human_skin.notes: Based on Tuchin et al. optical properties of skin

marble.notes: Carrara marble, approximate. Fine veining gives it medium local texture despite low saturation.

jade.notes: Order-of-magnitude engineering estimate, not a measured value — jade's translucency varies widely by grade/thickness. Grouped with marble as a similarly dense, moderately-translucent mineral.

soap.notes: Order-of-magnitude estimate for glycerin-type translucent soap. Colour hint deliberately broad/pale and overlaps wax/milk — auto-detection confidence for soap specifically is low; kept in the database mainly for explicit S1/S2 use when a caller already knows the material.

human_teeth.notes: Order-of-magnitude estimate. Deliberately NOT auto-routed to by detect_material_type() -- see that function's docstring. A raw colour match to 'pale and smooth' is indistinguishable from countless other objects without a mouth/face region proposal this pipeline doesn't have.

plant_leaf.notes: Chlorophyll absorbs strongly in BOTH red and blue for photosynthesis, so leaves don't follow the same 'red penetrates much deeper' story that drives skin's high ratio_min -- their translucency is concentrated more in green/near-IR. ratio_min is set conservatively lower for this reason; this signal is inherently weaker for leaves than for skin.

fruit_flesh.notes: Extremely high variance by fruit type (apple flesh vs. orange interior vs. melon) makes a single colour hint meaningless -- deliberately NOT auto-routed to by detect_material_type(), same reasoning as human_teeth. Kept in the database for explicit/future use once a real cut-fruit region proposal exists.
